questions.def: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: I enjoy ___ books in my free time.

questions.def: Decide is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: She decided ___ a new car.

questions.def: After 'good at', use the gerund form.
questions.question: He is good at ___.

questions.def: Want is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: He wants ___ a doctor.

questions.def: 'Stopped drinking' means you don't drink anymore.
questions.question: I stopped ___ coffee after dinner.

questions.def: Need is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: I need ___ for the test.

questions.def: Practice is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: They practiced ___ the piano.

questions.def: Hope is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: I hope ___ you soon.

questions.def: Offer is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: He offered ___ me with my homework.

questions.def: Avoid is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: She avoids ___ fast food.

questions.def: Plan is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: I plan ___ to Italy next year.

questions.def: Miss is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: I miss ___ my family.

questions.def: Afford is followed by an infinitive (to + base form).
questions.question: I can't afford ___ a new phone.

questions.def: Finish is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: He finished ___ his homework.

questions.def: Like can be followed by either gerund or infinitive.
questions.question: I like ___ by train.

questions.def: It's important to + infinitive
questions.question: It's important ___ every day.

questions.def: Hate + gerund
questions.question: I hate ___ late for meetings.

questions.def: Need + to + infinitive
questions.question: He needs ___ harder.

questions.def: Stopped to talk means paused another activity to talk.
questions.question: She stopped ___ him.

questions.def: Remember + gerund means recalling a past action.
questions.question: I remember ___ you last year.

questions.def: Regret + gerund means regretting a past action.
questions.question: I regret ___ that movie.

questions.def: Looking forward to + gerund
questions.question: He is looking forward to ___ you.

questions.def: Start can be followed by gerund or infinitive.
questions.question: It started ___ an hour ago.

questions.def: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: I enjoy ___ books in my free time.

questions.def: Want is followed by an infinitive (to + base verb).
questions.question: She wants ___ to the party tonight.

questions.def: Love can be followed by a gerund or infinitive, gerund is more common.
questions.question: I love ___ in the ocean.

questions.def: Stopped to do something means stopped an action to do something else.
questions.question: They stopped ___ coffee.

questions.def: Need is followed by an infinitive (to + base verb).
questions.question: I need ___ some milk from the store.

questions.def: It's important is followed by an infinitive.
questions.question: It's important ___ hard.

questions.def: Be good at is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: He is good at ___ the piano.
